notes: TOOLKIT PIN: the model card says the model is meant to be run through the olmOCR toolkit, so the toolkit is pinned like a model. Release v0.4.27 (2026-03-12) = commit 1e139a5ea61f1668164e6b63357d7284a8391615. Its `gpu` extra pins transformers==4.57.3 and vllm==0.11.2, and its own Dockerfile builds FROM vllm/vllm-openai:v0.11.2 — which is why that image, by digest, is the base here.

PROMPT: olmocr.prompts.build_no_anchoring_v4_yaml_prompt() at that revision. The adapter never inlines the text; lane A4 registers it as olmocr2_no_anchoring_v4_yaml_v1 and the runtime verifies at load that the registered text is byte-identical to what the installed toolkit builds. A drift between the two is a MODEL_LOAD failure, not something to paper over.

IMAGE HANDLING, and the one place this runtime deviates from the toolkit: the toolkit renders a PDF page with pdftoppm at a DPI chosen so the longest side lands on --target_longest_image_dim (default 1288). The arena feeds an already-staged PNG (masterplan 6.3 fixes one render pipeline for every model), so the adapter resizes that PNG so its longest side is 1288 with Lanczos and never upscales a smaller page. Resampling a raster is not the same operation as re-rendering a vector page; it is recorded in every receipt as resize_policy and it is a canary check, not an assumption.

FP8 AND WHICH POOLS ACTUALLY QUALIFY: the checkpoint is compressed-tensors float-quantized W8A8 (HF config.quantization_config.format = float-quantized, num_bits 8). Native FP8 tensor-core execution needs compute capability >= 8.9, i.e. Ada (RTX 4090, L40S, L4, RTX 6000 Ada) or Hopper (H100/H200). Masterplan 13.3 lists this lane as 4090/A40, but A40 is Ampere sm_86: on Ampere vLLM does not execute FP8 natively and may fall back to a dequantising path with different numerics and throughput, which would make it a different condition, not a slower one. A40 is therefore left out of gpu_pool_priority and the canary must print the resolved quantisation kernel before any Full Run.

VRAM BASIS: 10,061,929,760 bytes (10.06 GB) of FP8 safetensors from the HF blob listing, plus the toolkit's default --max-model-len 16384 KV cache and the Qwen2.5-VL vision tower. 24 GB is the floor; the canary measures peak VRAM.

Vendor-published olmOCR-Bench overall for this exact FP8 checkpoint under pipeline v0.4.0 is 82.4 +- 1.1. That is quoted from the model card, not reproduced, and this campaign scores it on its own pinned evaluator.

Role in the portfolio is benchmark-family reference baseline (masterplan 3.1): olmOCR-Bench is one of the three scored corpora and this is its family's own model. Read its olmOCR-Bench row with that conflict of interest visible.

PROMPT KIND toolkit (ARENA_CONTRACT D34). The registry file for prompt_id holds exactly what olmocr.prompts.build_no_anchoring_v4_yaml_prompt() returns at toolkit_revision 1e139a5ea61f1668164e6b63357d7284a8391615 (v0.4.27); adapter.load hashes the built text and fails closed on drift. CAUTION for the registry lane: A4's olmocr2_official_v1 entry records build_finetuning_prompt, the ANCHORED v1 prompt with a {base_text} placeholder. That is not this runtime's prompt. prompt_id olmocr2_no_anchoring_v4_yaml_v1 must resolve to the no-anchoring v4 YAML builder named in inference_config.toolkit_prompt_builder.

Framework-floor audit (2026-09-03, after the GLM-OCR canary died on an unrecognised model_type): the required framework floor, what the pinned base image actually ships, the action taken and the evidence URLs are recorded in provenance.json under framework_floor_audit. bootstrap.sh asserts the pinned framework versions and that the framework recognises this checkpoint's architecture before anything starts.
